items.t: Thanked "the 1,500 people that work in the judicial branch" on his appointment.
items.q: Funke in appreciation of his fellow candidates, he noted, “As I said to the judicial nominating commission, they are three excellent candidates.” “I want to thank the 1,500 people that work in the judicial branch,” Funke remarked.

record.t: Swore in 50 new Nebraska state probation officers on Oct. 22, 2026.
record.q: New Nebraska Probation Officers Sworn-In October 22, 2026 Read more about New Nebraska Probation Officers Sworn-In October 22, 2026 Fifty new Nebraska State Probation officers were sworn in by Chief Justice Jeffrey Funke of the Nebraska Supreme Court in a Capitol Rotunda ceremony on October 22, 2026.

record.t: Was appointed chief justice of the Nebraska Supreme Court by Governor Jim Pillen, moving into the role on Nov. 1 after Chief Justice Mike Heavican's retirement on Oct. 31.
record.q: Governor Jim Pillen announced his appointment of Justice Jeffrey J. Funke as chief justice to the Nebraska Supreme Court. Funke has served on the Supreme Court since he was appointed an associate justice in 2016. He will move to the role of chief justice on Nov. 1, following the official retirement of Chief Justice Mike Heavican on Oct. 31.

record.t: As chief justice, is the executive head of the Nebraska courts with general administrative authority over all state courts.
record.q: Funke is the executive head of the Nebraska courts with general administrative authority over all state courts.

record.t: Was one of four candidates a judicial nominating commission forwarded to the governor before his appointment as chief justice.
record.q: In early October, Funke was one of four candidates reviewed by a judicial nominating commission, all of whom were forwarded to the Governor for consideration.
